title: Ops Funnel Weekly: console + infra sync prep (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose: quick, actionable weekly sync to remove blockers between console product work and infra/serving runtime changes. Keep timeboxed, capture decisions, and leave with owners for follow-ups.

When: Fri 09:30-10:00 PT (15m core + 15m buffer for deep dives) — target 30m but keep strict start.
Attendees: console PM + eng, infra on-call rep, serving runtime owner, SRE rep, me (Vihaan).
Room: #infra-console Slack huddle or Zoom link in calendar.

Top-level goals this week:
- Validate canary rollback criteria for new traffic-split UI (console).
- Align on batch-sizing experiment schedule and telemetry hooks (serving runtime).
- Confirm fallback routing policy for eu-west region (infra).

Agenda (timeboxed):
1) 09:30-09:35 — quick context & metrics (me)
   - P50 / P95 tail for text-gen API (last 24h): 78ms / 210ms (hosted, 4k seq) — note slight P95 bump 03/09 02:00-04:00 UTC.
   - Token throughput: avg 110k tokens/s across pool; Dedicated pool at 85% capacity.
   - Console errors: 12 deploy-time API 502s (mostly transient) — stack traces attached.

2) 09:35-09:45 — Canary rollout for traffic-split UI (Marta)
   - Demo: new UI sends canary flag to route service (PR linked).
   - Needed: define automatic rollback trigger (current proposal below).
   - Proposal (quick draft): rollback if 5xx rate > 0.8% for 5m AND latency P95 increases by >30% over baseline for 5m.
   - Question: do we want separate thresholds by model family? (LLMs vs embeddings)
   - Action: Marta to write mini-runbook and add to Confluence (linked). Owner: Marta. Due: 2026-03-17. Status: TODO.

3) 09:45-09:52 — Batching experiment alignment (Jules / runtime)
   - Experiment A: dynamic batch cap 64 -> 128 during low-latency windows. Hypothesis: reduces per-token cost by ~12% with <10ms median latency impact.
   - Need probes in console telemetry to tag requests by batch-size and fallback count.
   - Danger: KV cache pressure on large batch sizes leading to P95 regressions.
   - Action: Jules to open INF experiment ticket with measurement plan + sample queries. Owner: Jules. Due: 2026-03-15. Status: In progress.

4) 09:52-09:58 — eu-west fallback routing (Owen)
   - Current: eu-west routes to a mix of hosted and dedicated. We saw a brief outage 03/09 where fallback to ap-south doubled cross-region latency.
   - Proposal: add an intermediate tier — regional spare nodes that accept read-only KV cache sync and can serve critical traffic.
   - Cost ask: small reserved capacity, estimate monthly $Xk. Need finance signoff if > $5k/mo.
   - Action: Owen to draft capacity/cost breakdown and a minimal config for routing policy. Owner: Owen. Due: 2026-03-18. Status: TODO.

5) 09:58-10:00 — Parking lot & quick wins
   - Quick win: add a console flag to disable streaming for specific routes (low risk) — demo by next week. Owner: Vihaan. Due: 2026-03-17.
   - Parking lot: rethink model variant fallback heuristics (defer to deep dive). Owner: TBD.

Notes to self / pre-reads to drop in calendar invite:
- attach PR: serving-runtime/pull/2748 (batching CPU profiling bits)
- attach logs: /s3/logs/hosted-api/2026-03-09-02-00.zip
- pointer: confluence/team/console-rollouts-2026 -> section "canary-safety"

Unresolved questions (call out in meeting if not answered):
- Do we standardize rollback thresholds across product lines or keep per-route tuning? pros/cons quick bullets prepared.
- Should batch-sizing be gated by observed sequence-length distribution per route? (short seqs might hurt)
- What telemetry retention do we need to support canary decisions (granularity, 1min vs 5min windows)?

Action item tracker (scratch, update after meeting):
- [ ] Marta — write canary runbook + Confluence section. due 2026-03-17. linked: confluence/team/console-rollouts-2026#canary-safety.
- [IP] Jules — open INF experiment ticket for dynamic batching; include sample traffic and regression checks. due 2026-03-15. GitHub PR referenced.
- [ ] Owen — cost / capacity plan for regional spare nodes for eu-west fallback. due 2026-03-18.
- [ ] Vihaan — add console flag to toggle streaming per-route; quick patch in console repo. due 2026-03-17. PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1120

Meeting follow-up plan (post-meeting):
- I (Vihaan) will update this doc with final owners + statuses and push to shared drive under "team/ops-weekly" (if consensus).
- For any action marked TODO, add to respective Jira and tag owner.
- If canary threshold changed, immediately update the canary-runbook Confluence page and ping #infra-console.

Scratch debrief (personal notes):
- Keep the canary criteria conservative for first 2 weeks. Prefer human-in-the-loop for rollout >10% traffic.
- Watch for similar P95 bumps that correlate with dedicated pool GC events — ask infra SRE for GC telemetry.
- Consider a small telemetry endpoint that returns batch-size + kv-hit ratio for sampled requests — low overhead sampling.

Done when: all items have owners + Jira tickets and runbook updated in Confluence.

Quick checklist before the call:
- [ ] Drop PR and logs into calendar invite.
- [ ] Ping Marta/Jules/Owen in #infra-console 30m before start to confirm attendance.
- [ ] Prepare a 60s summary of risk profile and one recommended fallback threshold.
